summary: You were in the hospital because your heart is weak and fluid built up in your lungs. You also had a lung infection called pneumonia. You are going home with four new medicines, and lisinopril was stopped. Weigh yourself every morning and eat less salt. Finish all of your antibiotic pills.

diagnoses.plain: Weak heart that does not pump well, with extra fluid (heart failure)
Lung infection in the lower right lung (pneumonia)
Kidneys were strained for a short time, now improving
Low red blood cells that is long-term

new.name: Furosemide
new.why: A water pill. It helps your body get rid of extra fluid so you breathe easier. You will urinate more; take it in the morning.

new.name: Losartan
new.why: Helps your heart and keeps your blood pressure down. It replaces lisinopril.

new.name: Empagliflozin
new.why: Helps your heart and your diabetes.

new.name: Amoxicillin-clavulanate
new.howOften: twice a day by mouth for 3 more days
new.why: An antibiotic to finish treating your pneumonia. Take every dose even if you feel better.

continue.name: Metoprolol succinate
continue.why: Slows your heart and helps it pump better.

continue.name: Apixaban
continue.why: A blood thinner that prevents clots from your irregular heartbeat. Watch for bleeding.

continue.name: Atorvastatin
continue.why: Lowers cholesterol to protect your heart.

continue.name: Metformin
continue.why: Controls your blood sugar. Keep taking it as long as your kidney tests stay stable.

stop.name: Lisinopril
stop.why: Stopped. Losartan now does this job, so do not take both.

stop.name: Spironolactone
stop.why: On hold until your doctor checks your kidney and potassium blood tests. Do not restart it on your own.

stop.name: Ibuprofen/other NSAIDs
stop.why: Avoid pain relievers like ibuprofen. They can hurt your heart and kidneys. Ask your doctor before taking any.

checklist.text: Take Furosemide 40 mg once a day, in the morning
Take Losartan 25 mg once a day
Take Empagliflozin 10 mg once a day
Take Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice a day until it is gone
Stop lisinopril. Keep spironolactone on hold until your doctor says otherwise
Weigh yourself every morning at the same time and write it down with how you feel
Get your kidney and potassium blood test (basic metabolic panel) before or at your first follow-up visit
Eat a low-salt diet: about 2 grams of sodium a day
Follow the fluid limits the heart-failure team gave you

call911: Severe shortness of breath, especially at rest
goToER: Legs or belly swelling up quickly
Making much less urine than usual
Fever or a cough that gets worse even with the antibiotic
callClinic: Fast weight gain or more swelling or breathlessness, following the weight plan your heart-failure team gave you
Any bleeding that worries you while taking apixaban
Before starting any new medicine, including over-the-counter pain relievers

followUps.why: Check your recovery, your kidney tests and your medicines
Check your heart failure plan and decide when to restart spironolactone

followUps.when: right away if your weight rises fast
followUps.why: Adjust your water pill before fluid builds up again

questionsToAsk: How much weight gain in a day or a week should make me call you?
When will you decide if I can restart spironolactone?
What should I do if I miss a dose of furosemide or losartan?
Which pain relievers are safe for me instead of ibuprofen?
When is my blood test, and do I need to fast for it?
